data.content:
On loan closure, an NBFC must release the original movable/immovable property documents and remove registered charges within 30 days of full repayment or settlement (para 35), and must state the timeline and place of return in sanction letters issued on or after 1 December 2023 (para 37). The borrower may collect the documents from the branch where the loan was serviced or from any other NBFC office holding them, as they prefer (para 36). If the borrower or a joint borrower dies, the NBFC must have a well-laid-out procedure for returning the original property documents to the legal heirs, published on its website (para 38). If the 30-day deadline is missed for reasons attributable to the NBFC, it must communicate the reasons for the delay to the borrower (para 39) and pay compensation (paras 40–41, which I did not read in full).

Sources: RBI NBFC Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025, paras 35–39 (Chapter III, section F). I did not check the mode of return (for example, courier or in person) beyond what is above, and I did not read the detailed legal-heir steps, because the corpus only sets the requirement to have a procedure.

content.text:
The corpus answers this only in part. Sanction letters must state the timeline and place for returning original property documents (para 37, for letters issued on or after 1 December 2023). Para 39 requires the NBFC to tell the borrower why documents were not released, or the charge satisfaction form not filed, beyond 30 days after full repayment, and para 41 makes the compensation rules apply to cases falling due on or after 1 December 2023, without prejudice to other borrower rights. I did not retrieve the compensation amount for property documents, so I cannot confirm it from the corpus. For gold loans, collateral must be released within seven working days of full repayment (para 58), with compensation of ₹5,000 per day of delay where the NBFC is at fault (para 69).

On the board-approved policy, the Responsible Business Conduct Directions require a Fair Practices Code and a grievance redressal mechanism, with disputes heard and disposed of at least at the next higher level (paras 7 and 8, Chapter II A.1). The Credit Facilities Directions require nodal grievance officers, with their contact details prominently displayed, for digital lending complaints (para 12). The loan agreement must also contain a grievance redressal clause and the nodal officer's phone and email, which may be a generic email if replies come within one working day (Annex I, part 2). Microfinance recovery grievances need a dedicated mechanism whose details are given to the borrower at disbursal (para 92).
